topicData.topic: Commission starts enforcing AI Act rules and new transparency requirements on 2 August
topicData.angle: Write from the specific facts and details in the source material provided.

postText:
Most organisations I speak to are still treating the EU AI Act as a 2025 planning item.

It started enforcing on 2 August.

The GPAI model rules are live. Transparency obligations are real. The AI Office is the enforcer with actual authority to act. This is not a consultation phase. The codes of practice are being finalised while the clock is already running.

I have watched this pattern before. A regulatory deadline lands and the people closest to the AI programmes assume legal is across it. Legal assumes the technical teams filed something. Nobody filed anything.

In a large telecoms or facilities management business that is running five or six AI initiatives across different functions, working out which ones are in scope is not a two-week job. It is months of internal archaeology. And that work should already be underway.

The "we'll figure out compliance later" posture just got significantly more expensive.

If you are in a technology or transformation role in a regulated European business, what does your AI inventory actually look like right now?

#EnterpriseAI #TechLeadership #DigitalTransformation
